_meta.purpose: Curated expert reference knowledge for two-stage chemical classification of crystal structures. Version 3 broadens coverage of elemental metals, intermetallics, pnictides/bismuthides, chalcogenides, simple halides including bromides/iodides, organometallic and coordination chemistry, organic molecular crystals, salts, solvates, hydrates, and reticular frameworks.
design_principles: Element presence alone is insufficient in grey zones.
Dominant anion/anion-group chemistry is a primary inorganic axis.
Hydrate water, hydroxide, acid hydrogen and organic hydrogen are distinct.
Family and analysis profile are separate.
Database stores chemistry knowledge; code owns algorithms and predicate evaluation.
Periodic rank/dimensionality is calculated later and is not hard-coded here.

COMPOSITION: For elemental substances, keep multiple candidates when bonding form cannot be inferred from composition.
For compounds, identify candidate anion systems but do not classify P/S/C solely by element presence.
Hydrogen alone gives no organic evidence.
Carbon alone gives no organic evidence.
Multiple plausible anion systems produce competing candidates/mixed-anion candidacy rather than a forced class.
STRUCTURE_REFINED: Use validated direct-bond and ligand-composition evidence.
Recognized oxoanion groups override naive carbide/pnictide/chalcogenide/halide routing.
Neutral H2O adds hydrate/solvate modifier and is not a second anion.
OH- is distinct from H2O.
Protonated inorganic oxoanions add acid_salt and remain inorganic unless independent organic evidence exists.
Mixed-anion requires distinct anionic species directly involved in coordination.
Organic classification requires organic carbon-skeleton or curated organic molecular-ion evidence; carbonate/bicarbonate/cyanide carbon is insufficient.
Zintl stays candidate-level unless polyanion and electron-count/valence evidence support it.
If evidence remains insufficient, return UNRESOLVED with alternatives.
Use exact curated group signatures when available; otherwise retain a broader parent family.
Do not infer oxidation-state-sensitive labels such as manganate versus permanganate from formula alone.
Complex halometallates and cyanometallates are classified as complex-anion salts before simple halide/cyanide routing.
Organic salts may contain inorganic counterions; organic classification follows a genuine organic molecular ion/skeleton.
Hybrid organic-inorganic crystals may retain both organic and inorganic subsystem evidence.
Simple Br-/I- halides must be distinguished from bromate/iodate/periodate oxysalts by direct ligand connectivity.
Arsenide/antimonide/bismuthide labels require pnictogen anion/polyanion context and must not override arsenate/antimonate/bismuthate oxygen chemistry.
Direct metal-carbon bonding is organometallic evidence; coordination through N/O/S/P donor atoms of an organic ligand is metal-organic coordination evidence but not necessarily organometallic.
Coordination polymer/network/MOF labels are assigned only after exact periodic analysis of the coordination graph; MOF additionally requires organic ligands and potential voids.
Metal-rich or high-coordination structures may remain generic intermetallics when Zintl/electron-count evidence is insufficient.
Homoatomic As/Sb/Bi and S/Se/Te subnetworks should be retained as alternative chemical representations rather than collapsed into only metal-centred coordination.

priority_rules.effect: Prefer inorganic.oxysalt over P/S/C/halogen families based only on central-element presence.
Neutral water gives hydrate, not mixed_anion.
HCO3/HSO4/HPO4/H2PO4 remain inorganic unless independent organic evidence exists.
Carbonate, bicarbonate, cyanide and carbide are not organic solely because C is present.
Promote mixed_anion only when distinct anionic species participate directly in coordination.
